59 // ── Severity taxonomy ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
60 /** The high-severity band (what the suspiciously-dry guard counts as "unresolved high-severity"). */
61 export const HIGH_SEVERITIES = Object.freeze(['BLOCKER', 'MAJOR']);
62 
63 /** Is this finding high-severity (BLOCKER/MAJOR)? */
64 export function isHighSeverity(f) {
65   return HIGH_SEVERITIES.includes(String(f?.severity || '').toUpperCase());
66 }

68 /**
69  * Count the still-OPEN high-severity findings — the `unresolvedHighSeverity` input the
70  * suspiciously-dry guard (c) reads. A finding is unresolved unless explicitly `resolved` (the Judge
71  * or a G9 debate can resolve one); an unresolved BLOCKER/MAJOR surviving to a fast dry is exactly
72  * the shared-blind-spot signature the guard fires on.
73  */
74 export function countUnresolvedHighSeverity(findings = []) {
75   if (!Array.isArray(findings)) {
76     throw new TypeError('countUnresolvedHighSeverity(findings): findings must be an array');
77   }
78   return findings.filter((f) => isHighSeverity(f) && !f?.resolved).length;
79 }

81 // ── Reading the FROZEN loop thresholds (N, K, M) committed in Wave 1 (I6) ──────────────────────────
82 /**
83  * The pre-registered loop thresholds the convergence + suspicious-dry logic reads. They were
84  * committed by a human in Wave 1 (preregistration.json); reading them HERE — never re-declaring
85  * them — keeps the loop honest (I6: the gate cannot be gamed by a locally-chosen number).
86  * @returns {{N:number, K:number, M:number}}
87  */
88 export function loopThresholds(prereg = loadPreregistration()) {
89   const out = {};
90   for (const k of ['N', 'K', 'M']) {
91     const v = prereg[k];
92     if (!Number.isInteger(v)) {
93       throw new HaltError(
94         `round orchestration needs the committed loop threshold ${k} (Wave-1 preregistration). ` +
95           `Got ${JSON.stringify(v)} — commit it before running the loop (I6).`,
96       );
97     }
98     out[k] = v;
99   }
100   return out;
101 }

103 // ── (a) the dry-round predicate · (b) the EMPTY-round guard ────────────────────────────────────────
104 /** The per-round reviews, accepting either a raw reviews[] or a round object carrying `.reviews`. */
105 function reviewsOf(round) {
106   if (Array.isArray(round)) return round;
107   return Array.isArray(round?.reviews) ? round.reviews : [];
108 }
109 
110 /**
111  * A DRY round: the tally surfaced NO new blocker (the trio's `tallyFindings().dry`). This is the
112  * convergence signal — but only a NON-EMPTY dry round counts toward convergence (see the tracker).
113  */
114 export function isDryRound(round) {
115   return !!round?.tally?.dry;
116 }
117 
118 /**
119  * An EMPTY round: the reviewers produced NO findings at all — nothing was actually examined. This
120  * is DISTINCT from a dry round (where findings were raised but none was a NEW blocker). I7 honest
121  * convergence: a run must not be able to "converge" by simply declining to look, so an empty round
122  * is invisible to the dry counter.
123  */
124 export function isEmptyRound(round) {
125   const reviews = reviewsOf(round);
126   const total = reviews.reduce((n, r) => n + (Array.isArray(r?.findings) ? r.findings.length : 0), 0);
127   return total === 0;
128 }

130 // ── G5 — convergence-until-dry, with the I7 honest-convergence guard + the T8 CLEAN path ───────────
131 /** The stamp a CLEAN convergence wears — explicit and DISTINCT from DRY, never conflated. */
132 export const CLEAN_CONVERGENCE_STAMP =
133   'CLEAN convergence: the panel raised ZERO findings for the required consecutive rounds — ' +
134   'nothing to dispute was found (DISTINCT from DRY, where findings were raised but none was a ' +
135   'new blocker). Clean requires MORE consecutive evidence than dry (cleanN = N + 1).';
136 
137 /**
138  * Build a convergence tracker: the run is CONVERGED after N consecutive NON-EMPTY dry rounds
139  * (DRY convergence), OR — T8 (2026-07-11) — after cleanN consecutive EMPTY rounds (CLEAN
140  * convergence, explicit stamp).
141  *
142  * I7 (b), REFINED not abandoned: an EMPTY round still does NOT touch the DRY counter — a run can
143  * never manufacture *adversarial* convergence by declining to look. But the OLD rule made a
144  * genuinely defect-free artifact structurally UNABLE to converge: zero-finding rounds counted for
145  * nothing, so reviewers were pressured to invent filler nits (the dogfood literally scripted one
146  * per round to terminate). CLEAN is the honest exit: strictly MORE consecutive empty rounds than
147  * dry needs (cleanN = N + 1 by default), stamped distinctly so the deliverable can never pass a
148  * clean run off as an adversarially-dry one.
149  *
150  * @param {{N:number, cleanN?:number}} o  N = the pre-registered dry threshold (Wave 1);
151  *   cleanN = the clean threshold (default N + 1; must be > 0)
152  */
153 export function makeConvergenceTracker({ N, cleanN = null } = {}) {
154   if (!Number.isInteger(N) || N < 1) {
155     throw new HaltError('makeConvergenceTracker: N must be an integer >= 1 (the committed threshold)');
156   }
157   const CLEAN_N = cleanN == null ? N + 1 : cleanN;
158   if (!Number.isInteger(CLEAN_N) || CLEAN_N < 1) {
159     throw new HaltError('makeConvergenceTracker: cleanN must be an integer >= 1');
160   }
161   let dryStreak = 0;
162   let emptyStreak = 0;
163   let rounds = 0;
164   let countedRounds = 0; // non-empty rounds — the only ones DRY convergence sees
165   const snapshot = (extra) => {
166     const dry = dryStreak >= N;
167     const clean = emptyStreak >= CLEAN_N;
168     return {
169       converged: dry || clean,
170       mode: dry ? 'dry' : clean ? 'clean' : null,
171       stamp: !dry && clean ? CLEAN_CONVERGENCE_STAMP : null,
172       dryStreak, emptyStreak, rounds, countedRounds,
173       ...extra,
174     };
175   };
176   return {
177     /**
178      * Observe one completed round. Returns the post-observation state, including whether this round
179      * COUNTED toward DRY (non-empty) and whether the run has now CONVERGED (and in which MODE).
180      */
181     observe(round) {
182       rounds += 1;
183       if (isEmptyRound(round)) {
184         // I7: invisible to the DRY streak (not incremented, not reset) — but it ADVANCES the
185         // CLEAN streak: consecutive genuinely-empty rounds are themselves evidence.
186         emptyStreak += 1;
187         return snapshot({ counted: false, empty: true });
188       }
189       countedRounds += 1;
190       emptyStreak = 0; // findings appeared — a clean exit must re-earn its consecutive streak
191       if (isDryRound(round)) dryStreak += 1;
192       else dryStreak = 0;
193       return snapshot({ counted: true, empty: false });
194     },
195     state() {
196       return snapshot({});
197     },
198   };
199 }

201 // ── (c) suspiciously-dry → probe-or-dissent (I1) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
202 /** The literal stamp a single-family substrate puts on an un-mitigable shared blind spot (I1). */
203 export const SHARED_BLIND_SPOT_STAMP =
204   'shared blind spot — UN-MITIGABLE on single-family substrate (I1): a same-lineage probe reproduces ' +
205   'the shared wrong consensus, so the unresolved high-severity finding is FLAGGED, not mitigated';
206 
207 /**
208  * Decide whether a converged high-stakes run is SUSPICIOUSLY dry and, if so, fire the
209  * probe-or-dissent — honestly.
210  *
211  * Suspicious (MASTER-PLAN crit-7 / I1) ⇔ the run is HIGH-STAKES, reached dry in FEWER than K
212  * rounds, AND still has MORE than M unresolved high-severity findings. Converging that fast with
213  * open high-severity findings is the signature of a SHARED BLIND SPOT, not genuine agreement.
214  *
215  * On a SINGLE-FAMILY substrate the only probe available is same-lineage, which by I1 reproduces the
216  * shared wrong consensus — so the fired probe CANNOT mitigate; it emits the un-mitigable stamp and
217  * reports `mitigated:false` (never a mitigation claim). A multi-family substrate CAN genuinely
218  * probe with an independent origin, so it may mitigate.
219  *
220  * @param {object} o
221  * @param {string}   o.stakesTier             governor tier (bin/stakes.mjs TIERS) — 'high' is high-stakes
222  * @param {number}   o.roundsToDry            non-empty rounds taken to reach dry
223  * @param {number}   o.unresolvedHighSeverity count of still-open BLOCKER/MAJOR findings at dry
224  * @param {string[]}[o.substrateFamilies=[]]  the model families actually reachable this run
225  * @param {{K:number,M:number}} o.thresholds  the committed K (suspicious bound) + M (finding bound)
226  * @returns {{ suspicious:boolean, fired:boolean, singleFamily:?boolean, mitigated:?boolean, stamp:?string }}
227  */
228 export function assessConvergenceHonesty({
229   stakesTier,
230   roundsToDry,
231   unresolvedHighSeverity,
232   substrateFamilies = [],
233   thresholds,
234 } = {}) {
235   const { K, M } = thresholds ?? {};
236   if (!Number.isInteger(K) || !Number.isInteger(M)) {
237     throw new HaltError('assessConvergenceHonesty requires committed thresholds { K, M } (Wave 1)');
238   }
239   const highStakes = stakesTier === 'high';
240   const tooFast = Number.isInteger(roundsToDry) && roundsToDry < K;
241   const stillUnresolved = Number(unresolvedHighSeverity) > M;
242   const suspicious = highStakes && tooFast && stillUnresolved;
243   if (!suspicious) {
244     return { suspicious: false, fired: false, singleFamily: null, mitigated: null, stamp: null };
245   }
246   // Probe-or-dissent fires. Honesty depends on the substrate.
247   const distinctFamilies = new Set((substrateFamilies || []).map((f) => (typeof f === 'string' ? f.trim() : f)).filter(Boolean));
248   const singleFamily = distinctFamilies.size <= 1;
249   return {
250     suspicious: true,
251     fired: true,
252     singleFamily,
253     // I1: a same-lineage probe cannot recover a correlated blind spot — single-family NEVER mitigates.
254     mitigated: singleFamily ? false : true,
255     stamp: singleFamily ? SHARED_BLIND_SPOT_STAMP : null,
256   };
257 }

259 // ── (d) G9 — conditional cross-origin debate ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
260 /**
261  * Detect CONFLICTING INDEPENDENT-ORIGIN pairs: the same finding (by stable id, G6) on which two
262  * reviewers of DISTINCT attested lineages reach OPPOSITE verdicts (one `affirm`, one `deny`). A
263  * same-lineage disagreement is NOT an independent-origin conflict (I3 — same lineage is one
264  * origin); plain agreement is not a conflict. Each review carries `{ lineage|family, findings:
265  * [{ topic|id, verdict:'affirm'|'deny' }] }`; a missing verdict defaults to `affirm` (a raised
266  * finding is an affirmation).
267  *
268  * @param {Array<object>} reviews
269  * @returns {Array<{ id:string, affirm:string[], deny:string[] }>} one entry per conflicting pair
270  */
271 export function detectOriginConflicts(reviews) {
272   if (!Array.isArray(reviews)) throw new TypeError('detectOriginConflicts(reviews): reviews must be an array');
273   const byFinding = new Map(); // id -> { affirm:Set<lineage>, deny:Set<lineage> }
274   for (const rv of reviews) {
275     const lineage = lineageOf(rv); // null when unattested
276     for (const f of Array.isArray(rv?.findings) ? rv.findings : []) {
277       const id = normalizeFindingId(f);
278       const rec = byFinding.get(id) ?? { affirm: new Set(), deny: new Set() };
279       const verdict = String(f?.verdict || 'affirm').toLowerCase() === 'deny' ? 'deny' : 'affirm';
280       rec[verdict].add(lineage);
281       byFinding.set(id, rec);
282     }
283   }
284   const conflicts = [];
285   for (const [id, rec] of byFinding) {
286     const affirm = [...rec.affirm].filter(Boolean);
287     const deny = [...rec.deny].filter(Boolean);
288     // A genuine conflict: an attested lineage affirms while a DIFFERENT attested lineage denies.
289     const crossLineage = affirm.some((a) => deny.some((d) => d !== a));
290     if (crossLineage) conflicts.push({ id, affirm, deny });
291   }
292   return conflicts;
293 }
294 
295 /** Should the G9 debate fire this round? Conditional on ≥1 conflicting independent-origin pair. */
296 export function shouldDebate(conflicts) {
297   return Array.isArray(conflicts) && conflicts.length > 0;
298 }
299 
300 function debatePrompt(pair) {
301   return [
302     `[researchPrime G9 — conditional cross-origin debate]`,
303     `Two INDEPENDENT origins conflict on finding ${pair.id}:`,
304     `  affirmed by lineage(s): ${pair.affirm.join(', ') || '(none)'}`,
305     `  denied   by lineage(s): ${pair.deny.join(', ') || '(none)'}`,
306     `Adjudicate which origin's verdict survives by EVIDENCE QUALITY (not by majority). Return the`,
307     `surviving verdict and the decisive evidence.`,
308   ].join('\n');
309 }
310 
311 /**
312  * Run the G9 debate gate. It is CONDITIONAL: it invokes the debate sub-agent EXACTLY ONCE per
313  * conflicting origin pair, and ZERO times when there is no conflict (done-when d). The injected
314  * `agent` is the call-count spy seam — every debate call goes through it.
315  *
316  * @param {{agent:Function, conflicts:Array, round?:number}} o
317  * @returns {Promise<{ fired:boolean, count:number, resolutions:object[] }>}
318  */
319 export async function runDebateGate({ agent, conflicts = [], round = 1 } = {}) {
320   if (typeof agent !== 'function') {
321     throw new HaltError('runDebateGate requires an agent() function', 'pass the injected seam: { agent }');
322   }
323   // 2026-07 efficiency: one debate per conflicting pair, all pairs CONCURRENT
324   // (Promise.all — same count, same order, same failure semantics as the old
325   // serial loop). RESEARCHPRIME_CONCURRENT_PANEL=0 restores serial.
326   let resolutions;
327   if (process.env.RESEARCHPRIME_CONCURRENT_PANEL === '0') {
328     resolutions = [];
329     for (const pair of conflicts) {
330       const out = await agent(debatePrompt(pair), { label: `debate:${pair.id}:r${round}`, role: 'debate' });
331       resolutions.push({ id: pair.id, resolution: out ?? null });
332     }
333   } else {
334     resolutions = await Promise.all(conflicts.map((pair) =>
335       agent(debatePrompt(pair), { label: `debate:${pair.id}:r${round}`, role: 'debate' })
336         .then((out) => ({ id: pair.id, resolution: out ?? null }))));
337   }
338   return { fired: conflicts.length > 0, count: conflicts.length, resolutions };
339 }

341 // ── (g)/(h) G8 — cross-lineage origin fusion (flagged-inert; routes through the SHARED module) ─────
342 /** The stamp G8 wears when it is inert (flag off / lineage-enum not committed). */
343 export const G8_INERT_STAMP =
344   'G8 cross-lineage fusion INERT (flag off or lineage-enum uncommitted) — no cross-lineage origin claimed';
345 
346 /**
347  * Is G8 enabled? Only when BOTH the explicit flag is on AND the closed attested-lineage enum has
348  * been committed (crit-5). The enum being pending (the Wave-7 default) keeps G8 inert regardless of
349  * the flag, because there is no attested set to fuse against.
350  */
351 export function g8Enabled({ flag = false, lineages = committedLineages() } = {}) {
352   return !!flag && Array.isArray(lineages) && lineages.length > 0;
353 }
354 
355 /**
356  * G8 cross-lineage origin fusion. Flagged-INERT by default (g): when disabled it claims ZERO
357  * cross-lineage origins and wears the inert stamp. When ENABLED it counts origins ONLY by asking
358  * the Wave-2 SHARED module `meetsQuorum` (h) — it NEVER tallies origins itself, so the I3 invariant
359  * (same-lineage agreement adds 0; only an attested distinct lineage adds +1) is enforced in one
360  * place. `attestedLineages` is passed straight through to the shared module (the committed enum).
361  *
362  * @param {Array<object>} reviewers  lineage-tagged reviewers ({ lineage } / stampRole { family })
363  * @param {object} [o]
364  * @param {boolean}        [o.enabled=false]
365  * @param {?Iterable<string>} [o.attestedLineages=null]  the committed closed enum (Wave 7)
366  * @param {?number}        [o.rhoHat=null]               learned correlation (Wave 9 supplies it)
367  * @returns {{ enabled:boolean, inert:boolean, origins:number, required:number, met:boolean, stamp:?string }}
368  */
369 export function g8FuseOrigins(reviewers = [], { enabled = false, attestedLineages = null, rhoHat = null } = {}) {
370   if (!enabled) {
371     return { enabled: false, inert: true, origins: 0, required: STATIC_QUORUM_FLOOR, met: false, stamp: G8_INERT_STAMP };
372   }
373   // THE SOLE COUNTER: route through the shared module. No origin number is computed here.
374   const quorum = meetsQuorum(reviewers, { attestedLineages, rhoHat, staticFloor: STATIC_QUORUM_FLOOR });
375   return { enabled: true, inert: false, ...quorum, stamp: null };
376 }
377 
378 // ── GATE-1 — independent-origins quorum for the round (the shared module, the sole counter) ────────
379 /**
380  * The round's GATE-1 verdict: independent origins among the round's reviewers, via the shared
381  * module. Identical routing to the engine's `gateOneQuorum` (bin/engine.mjs) — origins are counted
382  * in exactly one place across the whole engine (I3/h).
383  */
384 export function gateOneQuorum(reviewers = [], { rhoHat = null, attestedLineages = null } = {}) {
385   return meetsQuorum(reviewers, { rhoHat, attestedLineages, staticFloor: STATIC_QUORUM_FLOOR });
386 }

388 // ── (e)/(f) the active Synthesizer + Judge, behind a call-count spy seam ───────────────────────────
389 /**
390  * Orchestrate ONE round's adjudication layer (G4 Judge · G9 debate · active Synthesizer) over a set
391  * of lineage-tagged reviews, exposing a CALL-COUNT SPY SEAM (f): every sub-agent call is routed
392  * through a per-role counting wrapper, and the per-role counts are returned. G3/G5/G6 ride on the
393  * trio tally; GATE-1/G8 route through the shared module.
394  *
395  * @param {object} o
396  * @param {Function} o.agent                          the injected agent seam (the spy)
397  * @param {number}   [o.round=1]
398  * @param {?string}  [o.northStar=null]
399  * @param {Array}    o.reviews                        lineage-tagged per-reviewer reviews
400  * @param {string[]}[o.priorBlockerIds=[]]
401  * @param {boolean} [o.debate=true]  [o.judge=true]  [o.synthesize=true]
402  * @param {object}  [o.g8={enabled:false}]            G8 fusion options (default inert)
403  * @returns {Promise<object>} the round result + `counts:{synthesizer,judge,debate}` (the spy seam)
404  */
405 export async function orchestrateRound({
406   agent,
407   round = 1,
408   northStar = null,
409   reviews,
410   priorBlockerIds = [],
411   debate = true,
412   judge = true,
413   synthesize = true,
414   g8 = { enabled: false },
415 } = {}) {
416   if (typeof agent !== 'function') {
417     throw new HaltError('orchestrateRound requires an agent() function', 'pass the injected seam: { agent }');
418   }
419   if (!Array.isArray(reviews)) {
420     throw new HaltError('orchestrateRound requires a reviews[] array (the round\'s lineage-tagged reviews)');
421   }
422 
423   // Wave 1: reliability-wrap the injected seam at this injection boundary, so every
424   // adjudication call inherits typed retry + round-aware idempotency. The spy still
425   // counts ONE logical call per dispatch (it wraps the reliable seam); the wrapper's
426   // `round` keying guarantees NO cross-round dedup — two same-role calls in different
427   // rounds both execute. Transparent on the success path (one inner call per dispatch).
428   const reliableAgent = makeReliableAgent({ agent });
429 
430   // The call-count spy seam (f): one counting wrapper per adjudication role.
431   const counts = { synthesizer: 0, judge: 0, debate: 0 };
432   const spy = (role) => async (prompt, opts = {}) => {
433     counts[role] += 1;
434     return reliableAgent(prompt, { ...opts, role, round });
435   };
436 
437   // G3 ≥2-agree + G6 identity + G5 dry: the trio tally (the load-bearing reuse).
438   const tally = tallyFindings(reviews, { priorBlockerIds });
439 
440   // GATE-1: independent origins via the shared module (the sole counter).
441   const quorum = gateOneQuorum(reviews, { attestedLineages: g8?.attestedLineages ?? null });
442 
443   // G9 conditional debate (d): fires exactly once per conflicting independent-origin pair.
444   const conflicts = detectOriginConflicts(reviews);
445   const debateResult = debate
446     ? await runDebateGate({ agent: spy('debate'), conflicts, round })
447     : { fired: false, count: 0, resolutions: [] };
448 
449   // G8 cross-lineage fusion (flagged-inert by default; routes through the shared module).
450   const fusion = g8FuseOrigins(reviews, g8);
451 
452   // G4 Judge + Synthesizer: INDEPENDENT seats (the Judge reads the tally findings; the
453   // Synthesizer steers off the same tally) — dispatched CONCURRENTLY (2026-07-11; they
454   // ran serially for no reason, a free agent-call of latency in every medium+ round).
455   // Call counts, spy semantics, and results are identical to the serial path.
456   let judgeVerdict = null;
457   let direction = null;
458   const judgeP = judge
459     ? makeJudge({ agent: spy('judge') }).decide({ northStar, findings: tally.findings, round })
460     : Promise.resolve(null);
461   const synthP = synthesize
462     ? makeSynthesizer({ agent: spy('synthesizer'), northStar }).direct({ round, verdict: tally, northStar })
463     : Promise.resolve(null);
464   [judgeVerdict, direction] = await Promise.all([judgeP, synthP]);
465 
466   return {
467     round,
468     reviews,
469     tally,
470     quorum,
471     conflicts,
472     debate: debateResult,
473     g8: fusion,
474     judgeVerdict,
475     direction,
476     counts,
477     dry: !!tally.dry,
478     empty: isEmptyRound(reviews),
479   };
480 }
481 
482 // ── (e) Synthesizer steering, measured vs a token/round-matched control ────────────────────────────
483 // A heterogeneous reviewer panel that REUSES the trio roster (SHARK_ROLES) + angle rotation
484 // (angleForShark) for G3 heterogeneity, calling the injected agent once per reviewer. The verifier
485 // prompt is researchPrime's own (the contract surface anticipates this: makeSharkDriver emits a
486 // plan-level Shark prompt; verification reviewers need a different one) — but the ROSTER and the
487 // angle rotation are the trio's, reused not forked. A `focus` hint (the Synthesizer's steer) is
488 // surfaced to the panel so steered and control runs differ ONLY by whether steering is carried.
489 /**
490  * True when the engine must spawn the G3 panel rather than adjudicate supplied
491  * reviews: missing/non-array, empty array, or every reviewer has zero findings.
492  * (journal 0057 — empty findings arrays used to mean "operator will paste".)
493  */
494 export function isVacantReviews(reviews) {
495   if (!Array.isArray(reviews) || reviews.length === 0) return true;
496   return reviews.every((r) => !Array.isArray(r?.findings) || r.findings.length === 0);
497 }
498 
499 /**
500  * Coerce a live-panel finding onto the field-law surface: traces_to_north_star
501  * is the STRING 'yes'/'no' (booleans coerced — they silently demoted every
502  * finding when left as booleans, 2026-08-15). Anything else HALTs; never default
503  * a missing trace to 'yes' (that would inflate AXIS).
504  */
505 export function normalizePanelFindings(raw) {
506   if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
507   return raw.map((f, i) => {
508     if (!f || typeof f !== 'object') {
509       throw new HaltError(`panel finding [${i}] is not an object`);
510     }
511     let t = f.traces_to_north_star;
512     if (t === true || t === 'true') t = 'yes';
513     else if (t === false || t === 'false') t = 'no';
514     if (t !== 'yes' && t !== 'no') {
515       throw new HaltError(
516         `panel finding [${i}] traces_to_north_star must be the STRING 'yes' or 'no' (booleans coerced), got ${JSON.stringify(f.traces_to_north_star)}`,
517       );
518     }
519     const topic = typeof f.topic === 'string' && f.topic.trim() ? f.topic.trim() : `finding-${i + 1}`;
520     const message = typeof f.message === 'string' && f.message.trim() ? f.message.trim() : topic;
521     return { ...f, topic, message, traces_to_north_star: t, severity: f.severity ?? 'MINOR' };
522   });
523 }
524 
525 function reviewerPrompt(role, { round, angle, focus, artifact, northStar, heartbeatPath }) {
526   return [
527     `[researchPrime G3 verification reviewer — ${role.role} (${role.persona}); angle ${angle}]`,
528     `round ${round}: independently verify the claims and report any defect you can substantiate.`,
529     artifact ? `ARTIFACT (absolute path — read this file, do not guess): ${artifact}` : null,
530     northStar ? `NORTH STAR: ${northStar}` : null,
531     // G6 identity discipline: agreement is keyed on claim_id FIRST (falling back to
532     // the topic slug only when no id exists). Three reviewers wording the same claim
533     // three ways defeated the >=2-agree quorum once (journal 0001) — never again.
534     `For EVERY finding: when the claim you dispute carries an id in the artifact, set`,
535     `claim_id to that EXACT id (agreement across reviewers is keyed on it); always also`,
536     `set topic to a short stable phrase naming the issue.`,
537     `Return JSON { findings: [{ claim_id?, topic, severity, traces_to_north_star, message }] }.`,
538     `traces_to_north_star MUST be the STRING "yes" or "no", never a boolean.`,
539     `If you find nothing AXIS-serving, return { findings: [] } — an empty look is honest.`,
540     focus ? `STEER (Synthesizer): press hardest on — ${focus}` : `(no steering hint this round)`,
541     lookinAppendix({ heartbeatPath, northStar }),
542   ].filter(Boolean).join('\n');
543 }
544 
545 export { DEFAULT_CHECKIN_MS, DEFAULT_DEAD_IDLE_MS, DEFAULT_SILENT_KILL_MS };
546 
547 /**
548  * Recover the findings object from a live seat's reply. The drivers return `{ text, rec }`
549  * (the model's final transcript text), and a real reviewer answers with a ```json-fenced
550  * findings object, often after prose. Before 2026-09-04 the panel read `out?.findings`
551  * directly, so EVERY live seat reply was silently recorded as zero findings and an
552  * unparsed reply was indistinguishable from a clean look (three seats, three fenced
553  * findings objects, engine tally 0 — run report/researchprime-novelty, journal 0068).
554  * Returns { findings: Array|null, raw: string, parsed: 'object'|'json'|'empty'|'unparsed' }.
555  */
556 export function extractPanelFindings(out) {
557   if (out && typeof out === 'object' && Array.isArray(out.findings)) {
558     return { findings: out.findings, raw: typeof out.text === 'string' ? out.text : '', parsed: 'object' };
559   }
560   const text = typeof out === 'string'
561     ? out
562     : (out && typeof out.text === 'string' ? out.text : (out && typeof out.reply === 'string' ? out.reply : ''));
563   if (!text.trim()) return { findings: null, raw: '', parsed: 'empty' };
564   const candidates = [];
565   const fenced = [...text.matchAll(/```(?:json|JSON)?\s*([\s\S]*?)```/g)].map((m) => m[1].trim());
566   for (let i = fenced.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) candidates.push(fenced[i]);
567   candidates.push(text.trim());
568   // last brace-balanced object that contains "findings"
569   const key = text.lastIndexOf('"findings"');
570   if (key >= 0) {
571     let start = text.lastIndexOf('{', key);
572     while (start >= 0) {
573       let depth = 0; let end = -1;
574       for (let i = start; i < text.length; i++) {
575         const ch = text[i];
576         if (ch === '{') depth++;
577         else if (ch === '}') { depth--; if (depth === 0) { end = i; break; } }
578       }
579       if (end > start) candidates.push(text.slice(start, end + 1));
580       start = text.lastIndexOf('{', start - 1);
581       if (candidates.length > 12) break;
582     }
583   }
584   for (const c of candidates) {
585     try {
586       const j = JSON.parse(c);
587       if (j && typeof j === 'object' && Array.isArray(j.findings)) return { findings: j.findings, raw: text, parsed: 'json' };
588     } catch { /* try the next candidate */ }
589   }
590   return { findings: null, raw: text, parsed: 'unparsed' };
591 }
592 
593 const RAW_REPLY_KEEP = 20000;
594 
595 export function panelSeatAbstain(job, err) {
596   const msg = (err && (err.message || String(err))) || 'rejected';
597   return {
598     reviewer: job.role.role,
599     angle: job.angle,
600     lineage: null,
601     answerable: 'no',
602     panel_fault: msg,
603     note: `shark ${job.role.role} abstained (${msg})`,
604     findings: [],
605   };
606 }
607 
608 /** Seats that actually looked — not timed out, not thrown, not abstain-stamped. */
609 export function countSurvivingPanel(reviews) {
610   if (!Array.isArray(reviews)) return 0;
611   return reviews.filter((r) => r && r.answerable !== 'no' && !r.panel_fault).length;
612 }
613 
614 /**
615  * Spawn the heterogeneous G3 reviewer panel through the injected agent seam.
616  * Reuses SHARK_ROLES + angleForShark (not a second roster). Concurrent by
617  * default; RESEARCHPRIME_CONCURRENT_PANEL=0 restores serial (measureSteering
618  * matched-budget). Live path: run-rounds calls this when reviews are vacant.
619  *
620  * Swarm look-in (journal 0059/0060/0061): one hung/thrown shark ABSTAINS.
621  * Time-since-start is not a kill IF the seat is heartbeating. Silence is.
622  * Look in first; still silent → kill and respawn once. A talking seat that
623  * goes quiet dies on deadIdleMs. LOOKIN when the seat admits a rabbit hole.
624  */
625 export async function runPanelRound({
626   agent, round, focus, onCall, artifact, northStar, lineage,
627   checkInMs = DEFAULT_CHECKIN_MS,
628   deadIdleMs = DEFAULT_DEAD_IDLE_MS,
629   silentKillMs = DEFAULT_SILENT_KILL_MS,
630   heartbeatDir = null,
631   onLookin = null,
632 } = {}) {
633   if (typeof agent !== 'function') {
634     throw new HaltError('runPanelRound requires an agent() function', 'pass the injected seam: { agent }');
635   }
636   if (artifact) {
637     if (typeof artifact !== 'string' || !(path.win32.isAbsolute(artifact) || path.posix.isAbsolute(artifact))) {
638       throw new HaltError(
639         `runPanelRound artifact must be an ABSOLUTE path (journal 0002), got ${JSON.stringify(artifact)}`,
640       );
641     }
642   }
643   const jobs = SHARK_ROLES.map((role, i) => ({ role, angle: angleForShark(round, i) }));
644   const runSeat = async (job) => {
645     if (onCall) onCall();
646     const hb = heartbeatDir
647       ? path.join(heartbeatDir, `heartbeat-r${round}-${job.role.role}.json`)
648       : null;
649     try {
650       const prompt = reviewerPrompt(job.role, {
651         round, angle: job.angle, focus, artifact, northStar, heartbeatPath: hb,
652       });
653       const out = await superviseSeat({
654         run: ({ nudge } = {}) => agent(nudge ? `${nudge}\n\n${prompt}` : prompt, {
655           label: `reviewer:${job.role.role}:r${round}`,
656           role: 'reviewer',
657           round,
658           angle: job.angle,
659           focus: focus ?? null,
660         }),
661         getTrail: hb ? () => trailFromFile(hb) : () => null,
662         checkInMs,
663         silentKillMs,
664         deadIdleMs,
665         northStar,
666         task: artifact,
667         onLookin,
668       });
669       const extracted = extractPanelFindings(out);
670       if (extracted.findings === null) {
671         // An unparseable or empty reply is NOT a clean look: the seat abstains (honest
672         // tracker counts it as not-surviving), and the raw text is kept for the audit.
673         return {
674           ...panelSeatAbstain(job, new Error(`reply not parseable as a findings object (${extracted.parsed})`)),
675           lineage: lineage ?? null,
676           raw_reply: String(extracted.raw || '').slice(0, RAW_REPLY_KEEP),
677         };
678       }
679       return {
680         reviewer: job.role.role,
681         angle: job.angle,
682         lineage: lineage ?? null,
683         findings: normalizePanelFindings(extracted.findings),
684         reply_parsed_as: extracted.parsed,
685         raw_reply: String(extracted.raw || '').slice(0, RAW_REPLY_KEEP),
686       };
687     } catch (err) {
688       return panelSeatAbstain(job, err);
689     }
690   };
691 
692   if (process.env.RESEARCHPRIME_CONCURRENT_PANEL === '0') {
693     const reviews = [];
694     for (const job of jobs) reviews.push(await runSeat(job));
695     return reviews;
696   }
697   const settled = await Promise.allSettled(jobs.map(runSeat));
698   return settled.map((s, i) => s.status === 'fulfilled' ? s.value : panelSeatAbstain(jobs[i], s.reason));
699 }
700 
701 /**
702  * Measure the active Synthesizer's STEERING against a token/round-MATCHED control (done-when e).
703  *
704  * Both arms run the SAME number of rounds and make the SAME number of agent calls (the same panel +
705  * one Synthesizer direction per round) — so neither arm gets extra budget. The ONLY difference: the
706  * STEERED arm carries the Synthesizer's top suggestion forward as the next round's `focus`, while
707  * the CONTROL arm runs the Synthesizer identically (matched calls) but DISCARDS its suggestion
708  * (focus stays null). Any gap in findings caught is therefore attributable to STEERING, not budget.
709  *
710  * @param {object} o
711  * @param {Function} o.agent                  the injected agent seam (scripted in tests)
712  * @param {number}   [o.rounds=2]
713  * @param {?string}  [o.northStar=null]
714  * @returns {Promise<{ rounds:number, matched:boolean, steeringEffect:number,
715  *   steered:{caught:string[], agentCalls:number}, control:{caught:string[], agentCalls:number} }>}
716  */
717 export async function measureSteering({ agent, rounds = 2, northStar = null } = {}) {
718   if (typeof agent !== 'function') {
719     throw new HaltError('measureSteering requires an agent() function', 'pass the injected seam: { agent }');
720   }
721   if (!Number.isInteger(rounds) || rounds < 1) {
722     throw new HaltError('measureSteering: rounds must be an integer >= 1');
723   }
724 
725   const arm = async (steer) => {
726     let agentCalls = 0;
727     const counted = async (prompt, opts) => {
728       agentCalls += 1;
729       return agent(prompt, opts);
730     };
731     const synth = makeSynthesizer({ agent: counted, northStar });
732     const caught = new Set();
733     let focus = null;
734     for (let r = 1; r <= rounds; r++) {
735       const reviews = await runPanelRound({ agent: counted, round: r, focus });
736       for (const rv of reviews) for (const f of rv.findings) caught.add(normalizeFindingId(f));
737       // The Synthesizer runs IDENTICALLY in both arms (matched calls); only the steered arm USES
738       // its suggestion as the next round's focus.
739       const dir = await synth.direct({ round: r, verdict: { findings: [...caught].map((id) => ({ id })) }, northStar });
740       const suggestion = Array.isArray(dir?.suggestions) && dir.suggestions.length ? dir.suggestions[0] : null;
741       focus = steer ? suggestion : null;
742     }
743     return { caught: [...caught].sort(), agentCalls };
744   };
745 
746   const steered = await arm(true);
747   const control = await arm(false);
748   return {
749     rounds,
750     matched: steered.agentCalls === control.agentCalls,
751     steeringEffect: steered.caught.length - control.caught.length,
752     steered,
753     control,
754   };
755 }
